history.summary: Devi temple on Muzhakkunnu ('the hill that echoes', also called Mridangasailam or 'drum hill'), one of the 108 Durga temples of ancient Kerala traditionally installed by Parashurama. Legend: a mizhavu/mridangam drum fell from devaloka and Devi Saileswari rose from meditation to catch it; the dent is said to remain at the spot. The deity is worshipped in a trio form — Saraswati, Lakshmi and Kali — as Mizhavil Bhagavathi, and is the clan deity (kula devata) of the Kottayam royal family and of Pazhassi Raja, whose statue stands in the premises. Kathakali took shape here under Kottayam Thampuran, who penned the Ramanattam-derived texts Bakavadham, Kirmeeravadham, Kalyana Saugandhikam and Nirathakavachakalakeya Vadham at this temple. After Pazhassi Raja's death in 1805 the temple declined; it regained prominence after 2017 when former DGP Alexander Jacob recounted the panchaloha idol theft attempts, in which the thieves reportedly returned the idol each time after celestial interventions. name: Mridanga Saileswari Temple
town_description: Muzhakunnu (Muzhakkunnu) is a hill village in Kannur district, North Kerala, inland of Thalassery and roughly midway between Kannur and Kottiyoor. The name means 'the hill that echoes', tied to the Mridanga Saileswari temple legend. Once remote and known mainly to locals, it has grown in prominence as a pilgrimage destination, served by routes via Mattannur and Thillankeri.
